source.name: 362001066763+U-W06A(P3)V6.04-eu.bin
source.isa: Xtensa little-endian 32-bit windowed ABI; QCA4010 application; firmware LITBASE=0x00a39000

method.classification: bounded instruction-matched translation, NOT native Xtensa execution
method.decompiler: Fresh Ghidra12.1.4 project AtwLan37ab; Xtensa:LE:32:GreeLITBASE:default. Old ELF used only as processor import container, every memory block removed/replaced by independently extracted exact37ab segments. No existing project overwritten. All LAN functions actually decompiled; branches and loops checked against source instruction bytes. Ghidra incorrectly removes some zero-initialized request-list loops, so those are executed in bounded translation instead.
method.byte_assertion: Each translated instruction asserted against the exact mapped source bytes during every replay; segment hashes and original firmware hash rechecked by probe.
boundaries: ROM AES primitives independently named with matching SDK addresses; PyCryptodome substitutes each AES block primitive, not a claim to execute ROM/hardware AES. Firmware AES wrappers, key selection, padding, base64 and newline-conversion instructions execute in the translator.
libc memory and strcmp/strlen are Python memory/string boundaries.

cJSON parse/get/create/print/free calls are boundaries. Case-insensitive field lookup follows source0xa0de1c/0xa0d21c; ASCII vector serialization uses compact integer JSON. Parser reads first complete JSON value, matching source0xa0d7bc->0xa0d768(require_null_terminated=0). Unparsed trailing bytes are not decoded as text by real C; replacement decoding is confined to that research parser boundary.
Compiler integer-to-double and modulo helpers are arithmetic boundaries.
Clock, semaphore, socket-send and allocation/free callbacks are OS boundaries; outgoing UDP bytes are captured instead of using a socket.

Mainboard serializer0xa10a20 is a declared boundary after the actual command-byte-cache setter; this probe does not claim physical mainboard execution, incoming sensor calibration, full boot or Wi-Fi/cloud behavior.
Synthetic supplied identity/key/version/name and initially zero property cache; these are probe inputs, not recovered device defaults.

sdk.verification: Archive downloaded independently and both members re-extracted/rehashed in this research. Every six address matches the target source literal refs in0xa0cf28/0xa0cf94. SDK signatures take key,length16 and one16-byte input/output block; target wrappers iterate independent blocks with no IV/XOR/chaining: AES128 ECB.

contract.routing: All three actual emitted MIDs use same normal heater name/cache branch. 0x00a00278->0x0046b5f8; 0x00a0026c->0x0046b594 +0x64 equals same MID storage. The only alternate comparison is exact MID806004, not a separate model selector. See atw-properties_research.json for independent MID serialization/property probes.
contract.key_state: Existing 16-byte ASCII key supplied at0x464260. Selector0 uses it; nonzero low-byte selector uses source literal a3K8Bx%2r8Y7#xDh at0x44ba40. Bind validates inner MAC but does not generate/rotate key. LAN bind transport param=2; source decrypt rejects negative full selector. Controls dispatch requires full OUTER i=0, not inner i.
contract.outer: Require pack/i/uid/cid/tcid; tcid exact case-sensitive device MAC. Field lookup case-insensitive; operation values and property names case-sensitive. Incoming cid need not be a MAC. UID copied into reply, reply cid=device MAC and tcid=request cid. Scan starts with cleared context so uid0,tcid empty.
contract.reply_selectors: scan and bind outer i1 generic; status and command outer i0 bound. No GCM branch.

inner_reply_shapes.command: t=res,r=200,opt,p,val; no inner mac; p and val each echo selected requested values, not the final duplicate cache

contract.status: mac and cols required. Native wrong inner mac still selects response path and actual reply MAC. Known names preserve request order/duplicates; unknown names omitted. Exactly50 occupied slots yield empty cols/dat because counter falls through as0. Known table names not in the active930x selectors can read cache[-1] natively (e.g.EnvironmentTem); omit them safely rather than manufacturing zero support.
contract.command: opt and p required, val-only not a receive alias; inner mac not required. Numeric values copied into per-position requested array then nonnegative values byte-truncate into known control cache. Duplicate writes execute in order; last value retained in next status. Native unknown command names omitted from reply; all-unknown gives successful empty arrays. Native unequal opt/p allowed and reads stale/zero per-position values; do not emulate unsafe behavior.

limits.notes: Request receive bound applies original wire bytes. Outer pack text >=700 is left uncopied then decode/AES fails; proven valid684-character pack succeeds while704 and792 fail even below1024 wire bytes. Native status string31 into20 slots can overflow; native arrays and base64 reply have missing bounds. Safe runtime must validate whole batch/property names and bound padded/base64 reply before mutation; no source-derived outgoing wire1024 limit.
limits.reply_safety: For the1500-byte base64 output buffer require encoded ciphertext length<1500, independently of plaintext<1500. PKCS7 output max1120cipherbytes ->1496base64; hence at most1119plaintextbytes fits both native buffers. This is a safety bound derived from native allocations, not a firmware validation branch. Final outgoing UDP envelope can exceed1024; source does not impose1024 on replies.

safe_runtime_deviations: Reject unknown/unmodeled/read-only command batches, mismatched counts, non-integer/boolean/out-of-model-range values atomically rather than unsafe native partial/stale writes.
Reject ambiguous/malformed JSON, bad base64/padding and wrong inner targets rather than reproducing native coercion/unchecked-tail behavior.
Bound names to19 bytes and arrays to safe capacity; preserve/document native exactly50-empty behavior only if exposed.
Require ciphertext and padded/base64 reply to fit buffers before any command mutation.

unverified: No native Xtensa ISA execution, complete firmware boot, hardware AES engine, real UDP/Wi-Fi stack or physical appliance/mainboard calibration.
Startup random-key generation and non-LAN/cloud/timer/OTA operations outside this slice.
Other firmware builds deliberately not claimed equivalent.
Source JSON/libc/ROM/OS boundaries mean datagram vectors are instruction-matched translations, not captured physical packets.
